### Added
- **The Substrate worker pool gets a `PodDisruptionBudget`; the pool template's Karpenter knobs are documented and verified; a spread value is refused until the Substrate line carries it** (giantswarm/agent-platform#472). The platform runs every agent on the one `WorkerPool` (`kagent.substrateWorkerPool`, four gVisor workers, one actor each), and nothing guarded its workers against voluntary disruption: no budget selected them (the kagent namespace carried budgets for the controller and the database only), no annotation kept consolidation off their node — while on gazelle (2026-09-15) Karpenter had bin-packed all four onto one spot `m6a.xlarge`, so one consolidation or reclaim took the whole pool down: every turn in flight failed, every session waiting for a person was lost (its pause checkpoint is node-local, giantswarm/giantswarm#37795), new turns failed `no free workers available`. Decided 2026-09-15: the pool **stays on spot**, the workers get a **budget only**. New: `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.podDisruptionBudget` (`enabled: true`, `maxUnavailable: 1`, `unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow`) — a `PodDisruptionBudget` named after the pool in the kagent namespace, rendered by the connectivity chart the way muster-valkey's is (#439; the kagent chart has no budget template), selecting the worker pods by Substrate's `ate.dev/worker-pool: <pool>` label, so a voluntary drain moves one worker at a time (`ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS 1` with four Ready workers); the key never reaches the kagent release (`components.kagent.omitKeys`); the four budgets of the connectivity chart now share one spec helper and its guards (`agent-platform.podDisruptionBudget.spec`, the render unchanged). Documented in values.yaml, both READMEs and UPGRADE.md, unset by default: `template.annotations` `karpenter.sh/do-not-disrupt: "true"` (consolidation, drift and expiry never drain a worker node; a drift roll then waits on the NodePool's `terminationGracePeriod`) and `template.nodeSelector` `karpenter.sh/capacity-type: on-demand` (the only knob that covers a spot interruption; Karpenter-only — never on CAPZ, on-prem or a cluster-aws node pool), and the roll every `spec.template` change causes (the Deployment once, one worker at a time under the budget, turns in flight on a replaced worker lost, goldens untouched). **The render now refuses what `WorkerPool.spec.template` would prune silently** (`agent-platform.validateWorkerPool`): `topologySpreadConstraints` and `podAntiAffinity` — carried by no published Substrate release yet (the carried patch giantswarm/giantswarm#37797) and pruned by the CRD's structural schema, so a spread value looked applied and did nothing — are refused naming the key and the range until `components.substrate.versionRange`'s floor is the release that carries them (`agent-platform.substrate.workerPoolSpreadFloor`, empty until then) and forwarded verbatim from it on; any other key the template does not have is refused the same way (a typo was pruned in silence); the floor is read by the new `agent-platform.semverRangeFloor`. `kagent.controller.substrate.defaultWorkerPool` is marked inert (the kagent chart renders `SUBSTRATE_DEFAULT_WORKERPOOL_*`, nothing in the line reads them). `make verify-workerpool` asserts all of it: the budget from the connectivity chart of the working tree with the pool's selector and `maxUnavailable: 1`, gone with `enabled: false`, never on the kagent release; the annotation and the capacity-type selector reaching the kagent release and the resolved kagent chart's `WorkerPool` verbatim; the two spread keys and an unknown key refused; still exactly one `WorkerPool`. `make verify-disruption` counts the worker budget among the connectivity chart's; the golden render leaves it off on both sides. **Every installation with kagent on gets one new object** (the budget); no pod rolls.
